business_problem: Bazaarvoice needed a product-catalog platform that could ingest hundreds of millions of updates, keep search responsive across billions of products, and scale past index and disk limits without costly migrations or more operational overhead.
solution_summary: Bazaarvoice uses MongoDB Atlas and Atlas Search as the core data platform for its product catalog business. Atlas is the primary data store for the catalog team, which ingests and manages product data for syndication, content sharing, and sampling campaigns. Atlas Search makes that data searchable for customers and internal product teams, while sharded production clusters let the business scale horizontally as data volumes grow. When the team approached disk and index limits, including the 2.1 billion document ceiling for a single Lucene search index, MongoDB Consulting helped it shard the environment. That change reduced search replication lag from hours to near zero, preserved real-time updates, and opened the door for richer features such as autocomplete. By using Atlas and Atlas Search together, Bazaarvoice can keep serving product discovery workloads while freeing engineers to focus on new capabilities rather than database administration.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores and scales Bazaarvoice's catalog data for customer content, syndication, and product-discovery workloads.

solution_components.name: Atlas Search
solution_components.role: Indexes catalog data so customers and internal teams can search products quickly and support features such as autocomplete.

data_flow: Product updates are ingested into MongoDB Atlas, Atlas Search indexes the catalog for search and autocomplete, and sharded production clusters keep those updates flowing to customers and internal product teams with near-real-time freshness.
business_outcome: MongoDB gave Bazaarvoice near-real-time search freshness, room to scale toward 10 billion documents, and the freedom to add richer catalog-search features without increasing operational drag.
